implementation: Windows current-user DPAPI, CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN, no LOCAL_MACHINE flag, public application-domain entropy
storage: Identity::save_protected creates a new directory and identity.dpapi; Identity::load prefers protected storage and never falls back when that entry exists but fails validation
source_identity: existing diagnostic plaintext files are not automatically migrated or deleted

tests.adapter: 4 passed, including real Windows DPAPI boundary roundtrips and selected authenticator-corruption/truncation rejection
tests.identity: 3 passed: restored identity completes in-memory Noise KK exchange, existing destination is not overwritten, damaged protected file never falls back, decrypted invalid identity fields and oversized file rejected
tests.localhost_tcp: explicit protected_identities_authenticate_over_real_tcp passed with fresh test keys: DPAPI save/load followed by real localhost Noise handshake and encrypted probe/reply; 0.09 seconds
tests.localhost_initial_attempt: restricted execution rejected socket access with OS error 10013; rerun with authorized local-network execution succeeded
tests.workspace: all-target tests passed after restoring the prior missing-identity error context; the subsequently added TCP test was run explicitly
tests.apple_typecheck: workspace all-targets aarch64-apple-darwin passed on Windows; not native execution

review_fixes: Bounded file reads preallocate their maximum buffer to avoid reallocating secret-containing allocations
Public fields are decoded before the private key, with an erasable private-key temporary
Identity private field, protected plaintext buffers and computed validation shared secret are cleared on drop
limitations: No pairing-code protocol, automatic app-owned path, trusted-device list or UI enrollment is implemented by this change
Mac Keychain storage remains unimplemented; DPAPI envelopes fail explicitly on non-Windows hosts
Current-user DPAPI does not isolate other processes running as the same user; OS recovery/roaming policies may apply
Write failure may leave a partial destination; failure is reported, but atomic commit/retry semantics are not yet implemented
Targeted buffers are cleared; Snow internal copies, serde failure intermediates and all compiler/OS memory copies are not proven erased
OS DPAPI success still requires application record validation; selected corruption tests do not prove rejection of every possible metadata bit mutation
No Mac input injection, cross-machine discovery or visible smoothness claim follows from these tests
